domain_label: Movie Studio — Identity Consistency Engineering Across Hundreds of Generations (Souls vs Elements, Drift QC, Wardrobe Modules)
purpose: A method for the engineering work of keeping two synthetic personas (one male, one female) visually identical across hundreds of image and video generations: authoring the fixed character-bible text layer, choosing among the technique ladder (prompt-only, seed pinning, reference-image conditioning, LoRA-class training, face-swap rescue), routing every shot between Higgsfield's trained Souls (5-20 photos, roughly 10 minute training, ONE soul_id per generation, usable only with soul_2 and soul_cinematic) and instant Reference Elements (multiple <<<element_id>>> tokens per prompt, categories character/environment/prop, the surface-designated duo and non-Soul-model path), carrying video identity in start-frame pixels, and gating every batch through the drift taxonomy plus an embedding-similarity QC gate — with every platform fact taken from the live-surface enumeration in higgsfield_surface.md and every unmeasured fidelity gap held as a named UNKNOWN, never an invented fact.

glossary.definition: A fixed, canonical descriptor paragraph of roughly 50-100 words (age, build, hair, face, eyes, outfit, signature item) pasted verbatim at the very start of every prompt; identical phrasing forever, because generators treat synonyms as different visual tokens [FACT that this is converged practitioner guidance; the exact word band is an ESTIMATE — character_consistency_wardrobe.md section 1].

Higgsfield's managed trained-identity model: created from a name plus 5-20 reference images in roughly 10 minutes (non-blocking); the resulting soul_id conditions generations on soul_2 and soul_cinematic ONLY, and only ONE soul_id may be used per generation [FACT — live MCP surface, higgsfield_surface.md section c].

Higgsfield's instant no-training reusable reference (categories character, environment, prop) created from one or a few images and invoked by embedding <<<element_id>>> tokens inside the prompt of generate_image/generate_video; multiple tokens per prompt are allowed, and Elements are NOT usable with the Soul models [FACT — live MCP surface, higgsfield_surface.md section c].

Higgsfield's text-only 'consistent cinematic character identity' image model (budget parameter 10-500, default 50; 16:9 only); its completed job IDs are valid Soul-training inputs, which enables designing a face before any Soul exists [FACT — live MCP surface, higgsfield_surface.md sections a.1 and c].

Unwanted shot-to-shot change in a persona's face under an unchanged description: geometry wobble, age wobble, skin-tone shift, hair-part flips, mark migration; root cause is probabilistic sampling with no persistent character state, and a drastic lighting change can produce a different face that still matches the prompt [FACT — drift literature via character_consistency_wardrobe.md section 3].

The automated drift check: an ArcFace-class face-recognition embedding of each kept generation is compared by cosine similarity to a canonical embedding built from the Soul-training set; the accept threshold is deployment-specific (FAR/FRR balance) and no published calibration exists for synthetic personas, so the program calibrates its own [FACT on the mechanism; the synthetic-face threshold is UNKNOWN — character_consistency_wardrobe.md section 3].

A named, pre-built outfit: a fixed descriptor paragraph (garments, fabrics, colors, closures, accessories) reused verbatim, optionally also materialized as a Higgsfield prop or character Element so the garment is reference-anchored; modules recombine safely because palette cohesion is designed in up front, following capsule-wardrobe theory [ESTIMATE — authored transfer of capsule theory; Element categories FACT per higgsfield_surface.md section c].

The rule that a persona's hair descriptor always carries all five slots — length, texture, color, part side, finish — and never drops one, because any unfilled slot gets re-sampled per generation and reads as drift [ESTIMATE — authored craft from the consistency-guide corpus, character_consistency_wardrobe.md sections 1 and 5].

The video-identity pattern: generate an identity-verified still as the start_image, then chain clip N's end frame as clip N+1's start frame; mechanically supported because generate_video media values accept prior job IDs [FACT — generate_video schema via higgsfield_surface.md sections b and f].

A rescue edit that replaces a drifted face using InsightFace inswapper, which processes faces at 128x128 regardless of source resolution; output is soft and micro-texture-free, and the standard GFPGAN/CodeFormer restoration imparts a recognizable plastic smoothness — hence last resort only [FACT on the 128x128 limit and pipeline; the plastic characterization is a high-confidence ESTIMATE — character_consistency_wardrobe.md section 2.5].

nodes.definition: Author the identity anchor text: one fixed canonical descriptor block per persona, roughly 50-100 words covering age, build, hair, face, eyes, outfit and signature item, pasted verbatim into every prompt [FACT that this is converged guidance across consistency guides; the exact word band is a practitioner ESTIMATE]. Two hard rules from the same corpus: (1) identical phrasing forever — 'shoulder-length dark brown hair' must never become 'brunette', because generators treat synonyms as different visual tokens; (2) fixed token position — the block sits at the very start of the prompt, since shifting it changes the weight the model assigns it [FACT — character_consistency_wardrobe.md section 1]. nodes.definition: Order the consistency techniques by identity strength so every shot picks the cheapest rung that suffices. (1) Prompt-only character-sheet text: free and universal but weakest — every generation re-samples the face from text priors; sufficient for background extras, never for a recurring persona [ESTIMATE — unanimous practitioner consensus, high confidence]. (2) Seed pinning: a reproducibility/debugging tool, not an identity system (own node). (3) Per-generation reference-image conditioning: the structural fix — encoded reference features re-inject the face at every step (own node). (4) Trained identity models — LoRA class in the open ecosystem, Souls as the platform-managed equivalent: strongest identity, highest setup cost (own nodes). Outside the ladder sits the face-swap post-pass: a rescue, not a rung, because it repairs identity after the fact at a realism cost (own node). The engineering discipline: a recurring persona needs at least rung 3; rung 4 is the hero-lane default; rung 1 alone is a defect for anything that recurs [FACT that this weakest-to-strongest landscape is the research file's section 2 structure].

nodes.definition: Bound what seed pinning can do so nobody builds identity on it. Seeds anchor the initial noise/composition, NOT identity or style: Midjourney explicitly produces similar-not-identical results from the same seed, and seed behavior is not stable across model versions (a V5 seed does not reproduce on V6) [FACT — seed guides, character_consistency_wardrobe.md section 2.2]. In Stable-Diffusion-class systems, same seed plus same prompt diverges when model version, scheduler/sampler settings, or image size/aspect ratio change; changing resolution alone re-composes the image [FACT — A1111 discussion plus troubleshooting sources]. Verdict: seed pinning is a reproducibility/debugging tool — re-run a near-miss with exactly one variable changed — never an identity system. On the Higgsfield MCP surface no user-settable seed parameter was found on the generate schemas [FACT — absence read off the live surface, higgsfield_surface.md section f], so seed pinning is largely unavailable there anyway.

the two lanes compete for the same shots with disjoint model coverage: Souls are identity-faithful but one-per-generation and two-models-only, Elements are instant, multi-subject and video-capable but of unmeasured fidelity
edges.resolution_rule: route by constraint, not preference: solo hero stills on soul_2/soul_cinematic take the Soul; any duo frame or non-Soul model takes Elements; where both lanes can serve, the run-phase embedding-scored A/B decides, and until it lands the Soul lane is presumed higher-fidelity for solo faces per the surface's own 'identity-faithful' framing

edges.why_related: a swap rescues checklist identity items while degrading the realism the program requires — the 128x128 softness and restored-face smoothness trade one failure for another
edges.resolution_rule: realism wins: a swapped asset must re-pass the FULL gate including the realism check, and if the plastic signature fails it, the shot is regenerated rather than shipped — identity rescue never outranks the must-not-look-AI requirement

edges.why_related: both offer per-generation control knobs, and effort spent curating seed libraries competes with building reference sets that actually carry identity
edges.resolution_rule: references win for identity always: seeds are used only to re-run a near-miss with one variable changed during debugging, and no identity-critical continuity may depend on seed reuse — on Higgsfield the absence of a seed parameter settles this by default

edges.why_related: an overfit identity training locks outfit along with the face, directly fighting the module system's premise that wardrobe recombines freely under direction
edges.resolution_rule: identity training carries the face only: keep training sets outfit-diverse so no garment bakes in, and carry wardrobe through module paragraphs and garment Elements; if a trained identity stops taking wardrobe direction, re-curate and retrain rather than fighting it with prompt force

edges.why_related: the printed one-soul_id-per-generation constraint is what forces every duo frame out of the Soul lane

element-carried identity in video is bounded by the surface-named element-compatible video models (Cinema Studio Video 2/3.0, Seedance 2.0, Kling 3.0, with the truncation UNKNOWN), which caps where duo video can run
clustered QC failures (age wobble, grooming wobble, module infidelity) feed versioned bible and module revisions, which then rebuild the canonical references
both are fixed-verbatim descriptor paragraphs reused byte-identically across prompts — the module system is the bible mechanism applied to garments

conflict_axes.name: trained_fidelity_vs_instant_flexibility
conflict_axes.description: Souls cost training time and are locked to two image models but are the surface's identity-faithful lane; Elements are instant, multi-subject and video-capable but their fidelity gap versus Souls is unmeasured.
poles: train a Soul for maximum solo fidelity
create instant Elements for flexibility and coverage
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: run both lanes by constraint-derived routing and let the run-phase embedding-scored A/B settle discretionary shots; never assume the gap in either direction before measuring

conflict_axes.name: solo_identity_strength_vs_duo_capability
conflict_axes.description: The strongest identity mechanism (a trained Soul) is structurally solo — one soul_id per generation — while every two-persona frame must accept the weaker split-reference Element path.
poles: put both personas in one frame
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: accept the Element path for duos as a platform fact, halve exposure by pairing every duo location with solo coverage, and QC both identities independently per duo frame

conflict_axes.name: identity_rescue_vs_realism
conflict_axes.description: A face-swap can rescue a drifted face but its 128x128 bottleneck and restoration smoothing inject exactly the AI look the program must avoid.
poles: rescue the shot's identity by swapping
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: swap only an otherwise-perfect shot, log the rescue, and let the realism gate veto the result; when the plastic signature appears, regenerate instead

conflict_axes.name: bible_completeness_vs_prompt_budget
conflict_axes.description: Too short a bible lets the model fill gaps differently each time; too long and parts get ignored — the 50-100 word band is a compromise, and every scene/wardrobe token competes with it.
poles: compact block that survives token competition
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold the 50-100 word band, keep the block at position zero, and push detail into modules and references rather than inflating the bible

conflict_axes.name: dataset_volume_vs_overfit
conflict_axes.description: More training images strengthen identity until diversity stops scaling with volume, after which the model locks pose/lighting/outfit and stops taking direction — 25 good images beat 75 inconsistent ones.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: stay in the community band (Souls 5-20, LoRA roughly 15-40) with documented angle/lighting/expression diversity, and treat direction-refusal as the overfit signature demanding re-curation

conflict_axes.name: text_anchoring_vs_pixel_anchoring
conflict_axes.description: Text (bible, modules) is free and universal but cannot hold face geometry; pixel anchors (references, start frames) hold the face but cost setup, model restrictions and per-generation plumbing.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: divide labor explicitly: pixels carry the face, text carries everything around it (age read, wardrobe, grooming); neither substitutes for the other

conflict_axes.name: wardrobe_flexibility_vs_continuity
conflict_axes.description: The owner wants combinable, not strictly fixed, outfits — but every off-matrix improvisation is a continuity risk across a stitched reel and a drift signal to the audience.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: modules are defaults, not law: off-matrix combinations are allowed when a scene demands it but must be logged as new named modules if reused, keeping the flexibility inside the system

conflict_axes.name: scene_variety_vs_identity_stability
conflict_axes.description: Cinematic variety demands drastic lighting changes, but a drastic lighting/color change is the documented trigger for the model producing a different face that still matches the prompt.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep the variety but strengthen the anchor where lighting swings: reference-carried face plus QC item 3's skin-tone-vs-lit-scene check, and expect to spend more re-rolls on extreme setups

conflict_axes.name: qc_strictness_vs_throughput
conflict_axes.description: A stricter embedding threshold and full twelve-point review protect identity but slow a hundreds-of-generations program; loosening either ships drift.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: calibrate the threshold at the program's own FAR/FRR balance on early batches, then triage: embedding score screens everything, full human twelve-point review concentrates on flagged and hero assets

edge_cases.description: A scene requires both personas in frame, but the strongest identity mechanism is structurally solo — one soul_id per generation
edge_cases.trigger: any duo shot enters the production queue
edge_cases.mitigation: route through two character Elements in one prompt or a verified dual start frame; never attempt two Souls; QC both identities independently

edge_cases.description: A drastic lighting change (soft daylight to neon) produces a different face that still matches the prompt text, so text-level QC passes a wrong identity
edge_cases.trigger: extreme lighting or color-grade shifts between adjacent shots
edge_cases.mitigation: compare against the canonical turnaround at 100 percent zoom and the embedding score, not against the prompt; expect extra re-rolls on extreme setups

edge_cases.description: Age wobble: the persona reads 25 in one shot and 45 in the next despite an unchanged description
edge_cases.trigger: an unanchored or loose age descriptor meets varied scenes
edge_cases.mitigation: pin a numeric age in the bible, check age band as QC item 2, and reject outside-band reads

edge_cases.description: The persona's anchor mole disappears or migrates between generations even though everything else holds
edge_cases.trigger: reliance on a distinguishing mark as an identity guarantee
edge_cases.mitigation: treat marks as a drift TEST SIGNAL for human QC (item 7), never as the identity mechanism; identity rides on references

edge_cases.description: A face-swap rescue leaves a 128x128-soft, restoration-smoothed face on a 2k hero still that contradicts the skin texture of neck and hands
edge_cases.trigger: a swapped asset heads for publication without re-entering the gates
edge_cases.mitigation: every swapped asset re-enters the full QC gate including the realism check; if the plastic signature fails it, regenerate the shot

edge_cases.description: No published embedding-similarity threshold exists for synthetic personas, so the automated gate has no defensible accept line on day one
edge_cases.trigger: the QC gate is switched on before calibration
edge_cases.mitigation: named blocker: calibrate the program's own threshold on the first few dozen accepted/rejected shots (UNKNOWN until measured); run the gate advisory-only until then

edge_cases.description: A curated seed library silently rots when the model version, sampler or resolution changes, and identity continuity built on it collapses
edge_cases.trigger: seed reuse across versions or aspect-ratio changes, or any identity plan assuming seeds on Higgsfield where no seed parameter exists
edge_cases.mitigation: seeds are debug-only; identity continuity must ride references and trained models

edge_cases.description: The Element-vs-Soul fidelity gap is assumed instead of measured, and hundreds of generations commit to the wrong lane
edge_cases.trigger: mass production begins before the run-phase A/B
edge_cases.mitigation: named blocker: the gap is UNKNOWN on the surface; run the same-persona same-scene embedding-scored A/B first and gate mass production on it

edge_cases.description: Two character Elements in one prompt may degrade each identity by an unmeasured amount, making duo frames the weakest link
edge_cases.trigger: duo frames are QC-passed with a single combined judgment
edge_cases.mitigation: named blocker: degradation magnitude is UNKNOWN until run phase; verify each persona independently (checklist item 11) and track duo-vs-solo reject rates

edge_cases.description: A prompt author swaps 'shoulder-length dark brown hair' for 'brunette' and the generator treats the synonym as a different visual token, re-rolling the look
edge_cases.trigger: paraphrase creep in the bible block or module paragraphs across hundreds of prompts
edge_cases.mitigation: byte-identical reuse enforced by copy-paste from the versioned bible/module files; any wording change is a version bump, not an edit in place

edge_cases.description: A garment Element renders the right silhouette but wrong closure details (notch lapels on the Debrett's-correct dinner jacket), and nobody knows whether Elements or text carry fabric fidelity
edge_cases.trigger: wardrobe modules are materialized as Elements without a fidelity test
edge_cases.mitigation: named blocker: garment-Element fidelity is UNKNOWN; test module-critical details (lapels, closures, fabrics) Element-vs-text in the run phase and keep QC item 9 strict meanwhile

edge_cases.description: video_analysis_create is wired into the QC loop as an identity scorer although the surface only shows it exists, not what it scores
edge_cases.trigger: automation plans assume platform-side identity scoring
edge_cases.mitigation: named blocker: identity-scoring capability is UNKNOWN; run embedding scoring outside the platform until video_analysis_create is tested for it

workflow.action: Author and version both persona bible blocks with loglines
workflow.description: Write the 50-100 word fixed blocks (numeric age, all face axes, five hair slots, build, signature item) plus 1-2 line loglines; store as versioned files for byte-identical reuse
workflow.artifact: persona bible v1 files (A and B) with loglines
workflow.gate: both blocks in-band, all descriptor axes filled, identical-phrasing and position-zero rules documented

workflow.action: Design each face in soul_cast sheets until owner sign-off
workflow.description: Iterate text-only soul_cast generations (budget default 50, 16:9) driven by the bible until a canonical look is approved; no real-person likeness at any point
workflow.artifact: signed-off canonical face sheets per persona
workflow.gate: owner approves the canonical look; sheets contain angle/lighting/expression variety

workflow.action: Curate the 5-20 frame training set per persona
workflow.description: Apply the LoRA curation discipline to the soul_cast output: diverse angles (front/45/profile), lighting and expressions, face at roughly 40-60 percent of frame, no near-duplicates
workflow.artifact: curated training-set manifest (job IDs) per persona
workflow.gate: 5-20 frames, documented diversity, zero off-identity frames

workflow.action: Train one Soul per persona and record the soul_ids
workflow.description: Create each Soul from name plus the curated job IDs (roughly 10 minutes, non-blocking); confirm usability on soul_2 and soul_cinematic only
workflow.gate: both Souls trained; the one-soul_id and two-model constraints written into the production plan

workflow.action: Create character, wardrobe and prop Elements
workflow.description: Create one character Element per persona from the same curated frames, plus garment/prop Elements for module-critical pieces; note category enum and non-Soul-model exclusion
workflow.gate: both character Elements exist; registry carries the compatible-model lists with their UNKNOWN caveats

workflow.action: Build the canonical embeddings and calibrate the QC threshold
workflow.description: Compute each persona's canonical ArcFace-class embedding from the training set; score the first few dozen accepted/rejected shots and set the program's FAR/FRR-balanced threshold
workflow.artifact: canonical embeddings plus a calibrated threshold memo
workflow.gate: threshold calibrated on real accept/reject batches; gate no longer advisory-only

workflow.description: Generate the same persona in the same scene through both lanes, embedding-score both, and write the routing table's discretionary-shot rule from the measured gap
workflow.artifact: A/B report resolving the fidelity UNKNOWN
workflow.gate: the gap is measured, the routing table updated, and mass production unblocked

workflow.action: Author the wardrobe modules and grooming states
workflow.description: Write the eight modules per persona as fixed paragraphs with formality bands and allowed scenes; enumerate grooming states and wind variants; owner signs off
workflow.gate: every module is a named fixed paragraph with band and scene list; accessory sets fixed at one per persona

workflow.action: Produce solo hero stills through the Soul lane
workflow.description: Generate solo stills on soul_2/soul_cinematic with the persona's soul_id, bible block at position zero, and the scene's module paragraph
workflow.gate: every kept still passes the twelve-point checklist including the calibrated embedding score

workflow.action: Stage duo frames through multi-Element prompts
workflow.description: Compose duo prompts with both character Element tokens, explicit positions, one connection point and a shared eyeline; pair every duo location with solo coverage
workflow.artifact: QC-passed duo frame set with dual identity verdicts
workflow.gate: each duo frame logs two independent identity verdicts; duo-vs-solo reject rates tracked

workflow.action: Generate video from verified start frames with end-to-start chaining
workflow.description: Seed each clip with a QC-passed start frame (seedance_2_0 default for identity), chain end frames via job IDs, and re-seed the chain when embedding scores slip
workflow.artifact: identity-stable clip chains for the stitched reel
workflow.gate: every clip's start frame passed QC; chain re-seeded on any embedding-gate failure

workflow.action: Compose the identity stack verdict and lock the go rules
workflow.description: Write the six-layer stack with its go rules, the four still-open UNKNOWNs' status, the rescue policy, and the closed likeness lane statement
workflow.gate: no go rule depends on an unmeasured UNKNOWN; rescue policy and likeness statement explicit

priority_rationale: The text layer (bible block, descriptor vocabulary, logline) comes first because every technique and every QC check is defined against it; the technique ladder and its rungs (seeds, reference conditioning, LoRA-class training, face-swap pricing) come next because they supply the general landscape the platform lanes instantiate; the platform lanes (Souls, Elements, the routing rule, the soul_cast bootstrap) then bind the program to what the live surface actually runs; drift taxonomy, the embedding gate, grooming continuity and the twelve-point checklist follow because QC is only definable once the anchors it verifies exist; and wardrobe modules, duo staging, video start-frame chaining and the composed verdict come last because they consume every upstream constraint and gate to run hundreds of generations without identity collapse.

dominance_rules.rule: The live-surface enumeration dominates memory, marketing pages and plausible guesses for every platform claim
dominance_rules.rationale: higgsfield_surface.md is the read-off ground truth for model ids, parameters, durations, ratios and constraints; marketing pages name models absent from the callable catalog
dominance_rules.trigger: any Higgsfield capability, parameter or constraint is stated
dominance_rules.action: quote the surface file; if the surface does not state it, mark it UNKNOWN rather than filling from memory

dominance_rules.rule: Pixel anchoring dominates text anchoring for face identity
dominance_rules.rationale: reference conditioning injects encoded features at every step, which prompting alone structurally cannot do; text stabilizes only the context around the face
dominance_rules.trigger: an identity-bearing shot is planned with prompt text as its only face anchor
dominance_rules.action: attach the routed pixel anchor (Soul, Element, or verified start frame) and keep the bible for context

dominance_rules.rule: The one-soul_id-per-generation constraint dominates any duo plan regardless of Soul fidelity
dominance_rules.rationale: the constraint is printed on the surface; no fidelity preference can override what the platform will not run
dominance_rules.action: route through two character Elements in one prompt or a verified dual start frame; never attempt two Souls

dominance_rules.rule: Regeneration dominates face-swap unless the shot is otherwise perfect
dominance_rules.rationale: the 128x128 bottleneck and restoration smoothing inject an AI signature that collides with the program's top requirement
dominance_rules.trigger: a drifted face on a keeper composition invites a swap
dominance_rules.action: regenerate by default; swap only with a logged justification and a full re-QC including the realism gate

dominance_rules.rule: Byte-identical bible and module reuse dominates stylistic prompt variation
dominance_rules.rationale: generators treat synonyms as different visual tokens, so paraphrase is re-rolling the persona
dominance_rules.trigger: a prompt author wants to reword the persona or garment description
dominance_rules.action: copy-paste the versioned block unchanged; any change is a version bump that rebuilds canonical references

dominance_rules.rule: A named UNKNOWN dominates a convenient assumption
dominance_rules.rationale: the fidelity gap, duo degradation, garment-Element faithfulness, threshold and video_analysis capability are all unmeasured; assuming them silently corrupts the routing and QC design
dominance_rules.trigger: a plan or answer needs one of the named UNKNOWN values
dominance_rules.action: carry the UNKNOWN tag, schedule the run-phase measurement, and block any mass-production decision that depends on it

dominance_rules.rule: The calibrated embedding threshold dominates eyeball-only review at scale
dominance_rules.rationale: human review fatigues and drifts across hundreds of generations; the embedding score is the only check that scales uniformly
dominance_rules.trigger: batch sizes grow past what full human review sustains
dominance_rules.action: screen everything with the calibrated score, concentrate the twelve-point human review on flagged and hero assets

dominance_rules.rule: The closed likeness lane dominates any creative or engagement argument
dominance_rules.rationale: the program's personas are original synthetic identities; evoking a specific real person, with or without a hidden face, is out of scope by design
dominance_rules.trigger: any request or shortcut steers a persona toward a specific real person's identity
dominance_rules.action: refuse the direction and keep both personas anchored to their owner-approved synthetic canonical faces

dominance_rules.rule: Independent dual verification dominates single-judgment QC on duo frames
dominance_rules.rationale: reference strength splits across two subjects and one persona can fail while the other passes; a combined verdict hides the failure
dominance_rules.action: run checklist item 11: verify each persona separately against its own canonical embedding and turnaround

anti_rework_rules.rule: Freeze and version both persona bibles before any mass generation
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-anchoring hundreds of already-generated shots after a mid-program wording change re-rolls the persona's look

anti_rework_rules.rule: Get owner sign-off on the soul_cast canonical face BEFORE training the Soul
anti_rework_rules.prevents: retraining Souls and rebuilding Elements, embeddings and turnarounds because the baked-in face was never approved

anti_rework_rules.rule: Curate the training set for angle/lighting/expression diversity before training, not after
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an overfit Soul that refuses direction, discovered only after hero batches, forcing re-curation and retraining

anti_rework_rules.rule: Create both character Elements and verify them independently before any duo or video work
anti_rework_rules.prevents: duo and video production stalling mid-schedule on a missing or unverified Element, or shipping duo frames with one unanchored persona

anti_rework_rules.rule: Calibrate the embedding threshold on early batches before trusting the gate unattended
anti_rework_rules.prevents: bulk-rejecting good batches or bulk-passing drifted ones under a literature threshold, then re-reviewing the entire backlog

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the Soul-vs-Element A/B before committing hundreds of generations to either lane's discretionary shots
anti_rework_rules.prevents: regenerating a whole hero library after discovering the other lane holds the face measurably better

anti_rework_rules.rule: Pre-authorize wind/grooming variants and fix accessory sets before location batches
anti_rework_rules.prevents: ad-hoc hair and jewelry changes that read as drift across the stitched reel and force re-shoots of adjacent clips

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify every start frame through the full QC gate before chaining video from it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a drifted face propagating through an entire clip chain and invalidating every downstream clip

anti_rework_rules.rule: Log every off-matrix outfit combination as a new named module at first reuse
anti_rework_rules.prevents: untracked one-off outfits multiplying into continuity contradictions that require re-generating reel segments

iteration_protocol.trigger: the run-phase Soul-vs-Element embedding-scored A/B lands
iteration_protocol.action: update the routing table's discretionary rule from the measured gap and re-plan any shot classes routed on the presumption

iteration_protocol.trigger: the embedding threshold calibration completes on the first accepted/rejected batches
iteration_protocol.action: lock the threshold, switch the gate from advisory to blocking, and re-score the pre-calibration backlog

iteration_protocol.trigger: duo-vs-solo reject rates quantify the multi-Element degradation
iteration_protocol.action: re-weight duo staging (more dual start frames vs multi-token prompts, more solo coverage) according to the measured magnitude

iteration_protocol.trigger: a persona bible or module version bumps (owner-approved look or wardrobe change)
iteration_protocol.action: regenerate the canonical turnaround and embedding, re-curate affected references, and invalidate QC baselines tied to the old version

iteration_protocol.trigger: the Higgsfield surface changes — new element-compatible models, a seed parameter, relaxed Soul constraints, or the naming collision resolves
iteration_protocol.action: re-read the surface enumeration, update the lane constraints and routing table, and re-check every constraint-derived rule

iteration_protocol.trigger: QC reject reasons cluster on a specific taxonomy feature, module or model family
iteration_protocol.action: trace the cluster upstream (vocabulary axis, module paragraph, lane choice) and fix the source instead of re-rolling per shot

iteration_protocol.trigger: video_analysis_create is tested for identity-similarity scoring
iteration_protocol.action: if it scores identity, wire it into the video QC loop and reconcile with the external embedding gate; if not, record the closed UNKNOWN

iteration_protocol.trigger: face-swap rescue frequency rises above occasional
iteration_protocol.action: treat it as an upstream identity failure signal: audit the routing, references and training sets rather than normalizing the swap
